title: Golden-prompt monitoring for canaries, A/B, and shadow traffic
creator: Ethan Zhao
description: Scope: Build an automated quality-regression detection pipeline that runs curated 'golden' prompt sets against model variants during canary rollouts, A/B tests, and shadow traffic. The system should produce per-prompt and aggregated scorecards, surface regressions to the Console and alerting channels, and provide a simple auto-rollback policy that the rollout controller can enact when thresholds are exceeded. The pipeline must be tolerant to non-deterministic outputs, configurable per-model/task, and cost-aware (avoid running the full golden set on every single request).
acceptance_criteria: Golden prompt sets can be uploaded via Console or S3 and associated with a model-version and task
Per-prompt scoring pipelines produce time-series that are visible in Console scorecards
Rollout controller consumes scorecard deltas and canister pause/rollback signals when policy thresholds are breached
Alerts (Slack + PagerDuty) fire for high-confidence regressions and include links to diff artifacts and failing prompts
E2E test simulating a seeded regression causes the system to pause a canary and create an incident ticket
work_items: Design score aggregation strategy (weighted percent failing, median loss, and calibrated delta)
Implement evaluation runner service (eval-monitor) to execute golden prompts against live variants and compute metrics
Integrate metrics into existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> TS DB) and add Console scorecard UI
Add configuration options to rollout manifests for gating policies and auto-rollback rules
Add test harness: synthetic regression injection + integration tests for rollout behavior
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use deterministic evaluation runners with fixed seeds for stochastic models where feasible; fall back to distributional metrics (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity) for chat/open-ended tasks

Trade-off: Running full golden set synchronously on canary traffic is expensive. We will sample shadow traffic + prioritized golden subset for immediate gating and run the full suite asynchronously for longer-term alerts
Decision: Scorecards show both absolute metric values and delta vs baseline; gating uses delta with hysteresis to avoid flapping
Trade-off: Strict auto-rollback increases availability risk for noisy metrics. Include a cooldown window and require at least two consecutive windows breaching thresholds before automatic rollback
implementation_notes: New service 'eval-monitor' will pull golden sets from s3://redwood-golden-sets/<org>/<model>/<name>.json and cache locally; manifest in Console will allow editing/selection
Per-prompt outputs are stored as artifacts (golden vs candidate) and a summary diff is saved as a gzipped JSONL in GCS for fast retrieval and historical inspection
Metrics emitted: prompt_id, metric_name, metric_value, baseline_value, delta, model_version, rollout_id, region, timestamp
Integrate with rollouts: rollout-controller listens to /eval-monitor/webhook with aggregated verdicts and tags rollouts with 'eval_scorecard_id'
Expose API: /v1/scorecards/{id} returns summary + links to failing prompts (for Console and alert payloads)
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for scoring functions (similarity, token-level metrics) with edge cases for truncated outputs
Integration tests: deploy canary variant to staging that intentionally lowers semantic-similarity on a subset of golden prompts and assert pause/rollback
Load test: run eval-monitor against 10k prompts per hour per region to validate cost and latency; fallback to sample mode under heavy load
Flakiness analysis: run golden set daily for 30 days and compute per-prompt variance to build a 'flakiness' weight for each prompt
risk_and_mitigation: False positives due to metric noise: mitigate via hysteresis, minimum sample sizes, and combining multiple metrics
Operational cost: mitigate by prioritized subsets and caching of model outputs for unchanged inputs
Security/data leakage: golden prompts may contain PII. Enforce upload validation, encryption-at-rest, and RBAC on Console access
Rollback chattiness causing cascading rollouts: add global rate limits and per-team cooldowns
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ethan Zhao: Created initial ticket after post-mortem on REG-2026-02. We lacked early detection for a regression introduced in runtime-1.19. Proposed golden-prompt-based monitoring as a mitigation.
2026-02-25 - Priya Nair: Scoped MVP — prioritized a per-model 'smoke' golden subset (20 prompts) for immediate gating and a full suite for nightly regression sweeps.
2026-03-02 - Design review: Decided on delta-with-hysteresis gating. PM requested UI mock for Console scorecards; Design to produce mocks by 2026-03-08.
2026-03-07 - Engineering: Prototype eval-monitor runner completed. Initial integration test against a canary rollout (staging) shows consistent detection of a seeded semantic-similarity drop.
2026-03-10 - QA: Identified flakiness on 4/20 prompts across languages. Action: add per-prompt flakiness weight and increase sample size for those prompts.
2026-03-14 - Priya Nair: Updated rollout policy defaults to require two consecutive windows and a minimum of 15 evaluated prompts before auto-rollback. Preparing RFC for team review.
